On-demand single-name announcement index used by tools/mira_data: secCode orgId announcementId title disclosure date and the PDF URL, plus an event token derived from announcementType. Verified live 2026-10-02 (no cookie/token/JS challenge; plain browser UA is enough). Caveats that must travel with the data: pageSize is server-capped at 30; per-stock queries need an orgId (bulk map at /new/data/szse_stock.json, 6259 rows) because a bare 6-digit code returns zero rows; an invalid category code silently returns the whole market instead of erroring; announcementType is an undocumented hierarchical multi-label code list so unknown codes must fall back to other rather than being guessed; announcementTime is a UTC epoch so the disclosure date must be read in Asia/Shanghai or it lands one day early; the same PDF can appear twice under different announcementIds, so dedupe on (secCode, Beijing date, normalized title) and never on title alone. Event tokens come from announcementType, which is a pipe-delimited multi-label list rather than a single code; 012399 in particular is an ambiguous bucket (seen on 业绩说明会 records, on 投资者关系活动记录表 and on a 股东会通知), so ambiguous codes defer to the title and fall to other when the title says nothing either. Read on demand only - no bulk backfill or mirroring, per DATA_POLICY.

Aggregated sell-side expectations read on demand for one A-share name by tools/mira_data: consensus EPS per forecast year, the six-month rating distribution and the analyst target-price range. L5 consensus rather than an issuer fact - claim-taxonomy.md says a forecast describes expectation and never a reported outcome, so it may not anchor a reported-metric conclusion. The payload carries NO as-of timestamp, so the retrieval date is recorded as the vintage and point-in-time revision history has to be built by snapshotting over time. Vendor rating fields cover a six-month window. YEAR_MARK marks the actual year (A) versus estimate years (E); only E slots become claims. Single-name reads only - the same endpoint can return the whole market, which DATA_POLICY forbids.

source_name: National Bureau of Statistics data library (国家统计局数据发布库)
publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
notes: Official statistical agency source used by tools/mira_data for CPI, PPI, the PMI trio (manufacturing/non-manufacturing/composite), industrial value added, industrial revenue, urban unemployment, retail sales, fixed-asset investment with its three sector splits, real-estate investment, new-home sales and household income, plus GDP, and for **provincial** statistics (province GDP, GDP per capita, household income in annual and year-to-date quarterly form; 31-province and 71-city catalogues) through the macro_region family. The library was replaced on 2026-03-27 (公告: 关于新版国家统计局数据发布库上线的公告): the legacy easyquery.htm API now returns 403 and the successor is POST /dg/website/publicrelease/web/external/stream/esData with a JSON envelope, keyless and reachable from a plain stdlib client with a browser User-Agent and Referer - an earlier probe here wrongly concluded TLS fingerprinting was required, because it used GET against the retired paths. Catalogue and indicator ids are opaque UUIDs discovered through /new/queryIndexTreeAsync and /new/queryIndicatorsByCid; showType is mandatory (omitting it is a 500); unpublished periods are returned as the string 无 rather than omitted, so non-numeric values are dropped instead of read as zero; a long history can be split across several catalog ids, so records name the exact cid/indicator pair they read; and the release carries no publish timestamp, so the retrieval date is the vintage. Two documented gaps: total industrial profit is named by two catalog slices that serve no current data (one empty for 2011-2026, one stopping at 2011-12) so it is left out rather than approximated from a stale archive. An earlier note here claimed money supply was central-bank data and therefore absent; that was wrong and is corrected - the agency publishes M0/M1/M2 monthly (indicators named 货币和准货币 (M2) / 货币 (M1) / 流通中现金 (M0) in one catalog), and they ship as the MONEY_SUPPLY series, with the Eastmoney table as the cross-check.

source_name: China Securities Index Co. official index data (中证指数)
publisher: China Securities Index Co. Ltd. (中证指数有限公司)
notes: The index compiler publishing its own index data, used by tools/mira_data as the official benchmark denominator (protocol target benchmark_ohlcv in public-source-targets.md) and for index composition and valuation. Authority is registered as L2 rather than the class default L5 because the compiler is the authoritative source for its own index level and composition - the same override the SEC dataset rows use, recorded here and in notes rather than changed silently. Index history is keyless JSON and needs dates as YYYYMMDD (the dashed form answers HTTP 200 with an empty list). Composition, weights and the index valuation series are published only as OLE2/BIFF .xls workbooks, so reading them needs the optional dependency xlrd and degrades to csindex_dependency_gap without it; the workbooks are parsed positionally because the header row is bilingual. Two vendor facts are recorded on every workbook record: the weights file can carry a different date from the constituent file (observed 20260831 against 20260930), and the valuation workbook holds only the latest ~21 observations, so an index valuation percentile cannot come from a single read.

source_name: Shanghai Stock Exchange listed-company announcement index

Discovery pointers only. The adapter used by tools/mira_data returns headline, outlet, timestamp and URL for one A-share name and deliberately produces no canonical records: no claim_area family, no evidence-log rows, no manifest - media stays L4 context, matching the convention of the media sources already registered here rather than widening the protocol for it.
